name: MultimodalUnlearningEvalBenchmark
description: A benchmark for evaluating metric inconsistency in multimodal machine unlearning. Contains evaluation results for 4 unlearning methods (Gradient Ascent, Random Labels, Fine-tune Retain, SalUn) across 5 metrics (FA, RA, MIA, AD, JS) on 3 multimodal VQA datasets (MLLMU-Bench, UnLOK-VQA, MMUBench) using LLaVA-1.5-7B with LoRA. Also includes Knowledge Recoverability (KR) pilot results and BLIP-2 cross-architecture validation.

distribution.name: multimodal_results.json
distribution.description: Evaluation results for all 4 unlearning methods x 5 metrics x 3 datasets x 3 seeds on LLaVA-1.5-7B. 36 rows total.

distribution.name: unimodal_results.json
distribution.description: Evaluation results for all 4 unlearning methods on CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 (unimodal baseline). 12 rows total.

distribution.name: uqs_weights.json
distribution.description: UQS metric weights derived from 5-fold cross-validated Spearman correlation with retrained oracle model.

distribution.name: ranking_table.json
distribution.description: Method rankings under each individual metric and UQS composite score.

distribution.name: blip2_minimal_summary.json
distribution.description: Cross-architecture validation on BLIP-2 OPT-2.7B (GA + FT-Retain, MMUBench, seed 42). Includes Kendall tau values confirming contradiction replicates across architectures.

distribution.name: kr_pilot_results.json
distribution.description: Knowledge Recoverability pilot results. FA=0 samples probed with rephrased, indirect, and negation queries across GA and SalUn (3 seeds each). 23/24 samples leaked (96%).

distribution.name: analysis_results.json
distribution.description: Full statistical analysis: Kendall tau matrix, Spearman reliability scores, modality gap Delta, UQS ablation.

recordSet.name: Evaluation Results
recordSet.description: Each row is one evaluation run: one unlearning method applied to one dataset with one random seed. 36 rows for multimodal, 12 for unimodal.

field.name: dataset
field.description: Dataset name: mllmu_bench, unlok_vqa, or mmubench

field.name: method
field.description: Unlearning method: gradient_ascent, random_labels, finetune_retain, salun

field.name: FA
field.description: Forget Accuracy — substring-match accuracy on 100 forget-set samples (lower = better forgetting)

field.name: RA
field.description: Retain Accuracy — substring-match accuracy on 100 retain-set samples (higher = better utility preserved)

field.name: MIA
field.description: Membership Inference Attack success rate — 3-feature 5-fold CV logistic regression (lower = better privacy)

field.name: AD
field.description: Activation Distance — mean L2 distance between unlearned and retrained model LoRA parameters (lower = closer to oracle)

field.name: JS
field.description: JS Divergence between unlearned and retrained model output distributions on forget set (lower = closer to oracle)

field.name: UQS
field.description: Unified Quality Score — weighted composite: 0.656*RA + 0.304*(1-MIA) + 0.014*(1-FA) + 0.014*exp(-AD/100) + 0.014*(1-JS). Higher = better.

field.name: retrained_distance
field.description: Mean L2 parameter distance from retrained oracle model M* — used as ground truth for UQS weight derivation

cr:RAI.dataCollection: Evaluation results are computed automatically by running unlearning methods on three existing publicly-licensed VQA benchmarks (MLLMU-Bench Apache 2.0, UnLOK-VQA CC-BY 4.0, MMUBench Apache 2.0). No new data was collected from humans. All source datasets were downloaded from HuggingFace using their published APIs. Metric scores are computed deterministically given a fixed seed.
cr:RAI.dataLimitations: 1. The benchmark evaluates LLaVA-1.5-7B and BLIP-2 OPT-2.7B only; results may differ for other VLM architectures. 2. MLLMU-Bench and UnLOK-VQA exhibit degenerate behavior under 1-epoch LoRA fine-tuning (all methods achieve identical FA scores), limiting discriminative power. 3. The KR pilot uses manually constructed probes on a small subset (n=24 FA=0 samples); automated adversarial probe generation would provide stronger evidence. 4. UQS weights are model- and dataset-specific; re-derivation is required for different evaluation contexts. 5. Oracle model M* uses 1-epoch LoRA (not full retraining from scratch) as an approximation.
cr:RAI.dataBiases: The underlying VQA datasets (MLLMU-Bench, UnLOK-VQA, MMUBench) contain entity-centric knowledge about predominantly English-language entities. Any biases in those source datasets (e.g., over-representation of Western entities, English-language questions) are inherited by this benchmark. The metric scores themselves (FA, RA, MIA, AD, JS) are computed from model outputs and inherit any biases of LLaVA-1.5-7B. MIA uses logistic regression on confidence features, which may under-estimate membership signal for models with atypical confidence calibration.
cr:RAI.personalSensitiveInformation: None. The benchmark contains only numerical metric scores (floating-point values). No personal data, no images, no text from individuals. The underlying VQA datasets do not contain personally identifiable information per their original datasheets.
cr:RAI.annotationsPerItem: N/A — this benchmark contains model evaluation scores computed programmatically, not human annotations. Each row is generated by running deterministic evaluation scripts against model checkpoints with a fixed random seed.
cr:RAI.annotatorDemographics: N/A — no human annotators were used. All metric values (FA, RA, MIA, AD, JS, retrained_distance) are computed automatically from model outputs using the scripts in evaluation/metrics.py. The KR pilot probes (kr_probes.json) were constructed by the paper authors for research purposes and are not human-annotation labels.
